newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France to open German air trucking hub.
newsitem.headline: Air France to open German air trucking hub.

text.p: Air France said it will open its German air cargo road trucking hub at Hahn airport on July 1.
Air cargo will be trucked from throughout Germany to the former U.S. military airport in Rhineland-Palatinate and sorted for onward transportation to Paris.
In a joint invitation to the opening ceremony, Air France and the Hahn airport authority said the airline had chosen the location on time and cost grounds.
But expansion opportunities, good transport links and the 24-hour operations possible at Hahn airport had also been decisive factors, they added.
The hub includes a 6,000 sq m freight terminal able to handle up to 60,000 tonnes of airfreight a year and office space.
Air France currently trucks most of its German airfreight via Frankfurt airport to Paris.
Hahn airport is seeking to establish itself as an airport for heavylift cargo and logistics operations.
